listing.name: SSMSControllerEx - Controller Support
listing.summary: Full controller support for Starsector. Currently supports Xbox 360, PS4, Nintendo Switch, and Steam Deck. Campaign support is nearly complete for the most common UI's, but for late-game stuff like colony management UI's, don't expect much.
listing.aiSummary: Adds full controller support for Starsector, allowing joystick or d-pad navigation of UI elements and specialized controls for campaign and combat views.

description:
SSMSControllerEx - Controller support for Starsector

This mod adds full support for using a controller in Starsector. On screens that show UIs with clickable buttons, the mod allows you to either use the joystick to move a fake mouse cursor around the screen to click a button, or use the d-pad to navigate between the clickable elements, then the A button to press a button. Special controls exist to give the player more precise control in the campaign view and the combat view, more details below. Should support about 95% of the screens in the game. Expect hiccups here or there. I have not completed the game. But I've played about 10 hours on my personal Steam Deck using only this mod and I feel rather confident in it at this point. Based off the good work by razuhl with his

SSMSController mod

Shout out to my fellow couch gamers!

Depends on LunaLib and LazyLib.

Download v2.0.3[0.98a-RC8]

Screenshots:

Spoiler The on-screen mappings for the title screen

The on-screen mappings in the campaign view

The on-screen mappings in the deployment view

On-screen mappings in combat

The pause menu in combat

The trade UI with bindings visible

The controller settings UI, accessible from the title screen by clicking the "Controller Settings" button[close]Button mappings:

Spoiler Generic inputs (Title screen, most UIs and menus and dialog boxes)

Campaign UI (unpaused)

Campaign UI (paused)

Campaign tabs, generic

Trade/Cargo tab inputs

Combat controls (default, steering relative to ship position)

Combat controls (cardinal steering, steering controls are absolute)

[close]Changelog (v2.0.3)

Spoiler- When you click a stack in the trade UI, the logic that moves the mouse to the opposite cargo doesn't account for scrolling, leading to cases where the mouse ends up above or below the grid and you can only press B to cancel. Now the appropriate cell to be moused over is scrolled into view before moving the mouse.

- Pressing 'X' on any map control now does a right-click, as in "Lay in course"

- Clicking L3 on the Trade UI now sends a right-click, as in "Learn mod/blueprint/etc"[close]

Installation (WINDOWS ONLY)

After unzipping the mod contents to mods\SSMSControllerEx , from the SSMSControllerEx\native\windows folder, copy SSMSControllerExNative.dll to the folder Starsector\starsector-core\native\windows . If your controller worked in the previous version of SSMSControllerEx you shouldn't notice any difference in behavior. This step should ensure that just about any controller with a layout similar to an X-Box controller should work with the mod. To be clear, this is ONLY necessary on windows.

Installation (STEAM DECK ONLY)

After unzipping the mod contents to mods/SSMSControllerEx, replace the jinput.jar under the starsector folder with the one

here

and replace libjinput-linux64.so under starsector/native/linux with

this one

the version shipped with Starsector has some bugs with interpreting the buttons/axes from the Steam Deck controller.

Known bugs:

Spoiler

The ship info shows over the menu screen in the combat viewStarsector's LWJGL library that it uses does not work well with the Switch Pro controller and some other controllers like the Steam Deck in Desktop mode. You have to add Starsector as a non-steam game and enable Steam Input for Starsector, this will emulate an XBox controller that works with the game. Not something I can fix unfortunately.

[close]

Current controllers supported:

- On Linux and Windows, all controllers supported under the

SDL mapping file

should be supported by this mod. Big thanks to this team for their great work.

If your controller is unsupported, a special button auto-mapper UI will appear on the title screen prompting you to enter the button corresponding with a given button icon on the screen. Once it's finished, the controller should work. The only caveat is that it doesn't save the mappings, so you'll need to re-enter them every time you start the game.

- there is also the wonderful controller settings UI, see the screenshots, this should be very helpful for setting the active controller, and changing the mappings.[/list][/list]
